The bubble pops: one frame of smear, then the overwhelm state arrives through the lag chain, light first, glass second. The gadget stands free, dial wide. It projects: stalks shoot up across the field, arches drop in, rings spin out, patches tile outward, beads scatter. Each arrives on twos, staggered 3, until nothing is staggered anymore and everything arrives at once (the one permitted violation of law 1, as the point of the beat). Codex's glyph flickers; Clawd's eyes narrow. The frame fills toward the maximalist painting. Hold 12 at full.

data.prose: The human reaches for a stalk and a patch: anticipation, action, contact. The join fails: no pulse, the stalk slides back. Second try with an arch: the arch stays dark, the piece returns. A stack of patches collapses (three pieces, staggered 3, each a settle with no hold). The radiance goes noisy, grain up, the single emitter lost among projections. The companions wince (one boil variant held). Hold 16 on the mess.

Through it: the environment already assembled, rings, arches, stalks, patches, string, refracted and diffused, someplace else. Outside the frame the projections dim through the lag; inside, the emitter narrows to one piece. Hold 20 on the view through the frame. The human looks from the mess to the frame.

data.title: What happens in beat 4
data.text: 1. Slump: the human is still bent from the failed joins, cloak heavy, the light lost on the floor; hold. 2. The frame rises at the edge, Clawd lifting it from the hand's side; the light moves before the human does: the floor glow dies and the frame's interior lights; the human turns toward it with a small anticipation away first. 3. Rise: the human stands up out of the cloak, which drops as a heap and stays there; weight on contact: the body settles, then the cloth settles after. 4. One step toward the frame, then the threshold pause: the heel tap into the shoe, the gesture no one needs, so the body is real before it goes through. 5. Codex, small, nudges the cloak heap aside with one foot: the beat's one gag. 6. Through: the human goes alone, framed small inside the frame's light; the guides follow into the art world.

items.label: p002 Materials as a contract, not a 3D engine

data.title: Materials as a contract, not a 3D engine
data.text: Every asset declares a material (cloth, hair, glass, light, paper, box, bubble, line) in v3/materials.json, and a material carries the drawn-animation properties that are re-derived by hand today: mass class, follow-through lag in frames, settle frames and overshoot, drag on arcs, boil amplitude, shadow class (stipple), and for transmissive ones refraction and diffusion. The pose step's secondaries are generated from the material, not written per pose: a cloak lags the body by its declared frames and settles after it; hair lags less; glass displaces what is behind it. A follow-through probe with a control refuses a secondary that settles before its primary. No simulation: the properties are the twelve principles as numbers, deterministic and cached like everything else; the GPU glass pass and the ARAP mesh stay as they are. Test case: the cloak drop in beat 4 (p001 step 3) and the heel tap settle (step 4).

items.label: p003 Light as a signed-distance shader layer, no engine

data.title: Light as a signed-distance shader layer, no engine
data.text: Keep Remotion and Three. Borrow Godot's 2D light model (a per-pixel light function, occluder shadows, a viewport signed-distance field for soft shadows) and Spine's physics-constraint shape (a secondary derived from a few numbers on the bone) as techniques, not engines. Light becomes one cached layer: the drawn roles form an occluder mask, a jump-flood pass turns it into a distance field, the emitter's volume is the field's falloff, its shadow is a march toward the emitter with the penumbra from the distance along the ray, one bounce level makes lit edges weak secondary emitters in the role's hue shifted toward the pair, and the existing stipple quantises the result so the shading law (dither, not ramps) is untouched. Glass reads the same buffer. The layer is hashed on the occluder masks, the emitter path, the material table and the backend name. Materials (p002) gain occluder class, bounce albedo and shadow class, so one file drives motion and radiance. Every engine and runtime (r3f, drei, postprocessing, Pixi, Babylon, Godot web export, Unity, Spine/Rive runtimes, Matter, Rapier, Lottie) is avoided; Blender stays the optional renderer (D62); radiance cascades proper is a trial only if a shot needs more than one emitter and two bounces. Order: p002 first for beat 4, then this layer before the world beats. Recommendation receipt: chain-tech_recommendation#1 (second pass, 2026-10-18).

items.label: p004 A direction vocabulary: one skill, referenced by the prompts, enforced by a gate

data.title: A direction vocabulary: one skill, referenced by the prompts, enforced by a gate
data.text: Stylistic intent is controlled by making every property value, ruling and interview question carry a word from one controlled vocabulary of cinematography and direction, and by recording which reference led to which change. The vocabulary is a skill (project-agnostic, like the animation chains), kept as a machine-readable JSON with a generated reference table; the prompts reference the skill and never restate it; a gate probe refuses a ruling, proposal, pose sheet facet or material value whose intent word is outside the vocabulary. The interview and the rulings take one fixed form each.

before.note: rulings are free prose (D35-D95 use mixed words: 'reverent', 'floods', 'Turrell blue', 'gentle gag'); interview questions are written fresh each round; the board's facets are a vocabulary for references only; material values would be bare numbers with no intent attached; a change's reason lives in the commit message

after.skill: ~/.claude/skills/animation-direction (exported to clients through skills-sync): SKILL.md = the interview protocol and the ruling form; references/vocabulary.json = the controlled terms by domain (shot size, angle, move, staging, timing, acting register, light role and quality, material intent, transition), each with a one-line definition and the lane or property it governs; references/vocabulary.md generated from the JSON
after.project: media/showcase/v3/vocabulary-overrides.json: the film's own words (register names, the hue-pair names, the worlds) layered over the skill's terms, the way card-schema.json overrides the inspiration facets
after.prompts: animation_* and showcase_* system messages gain one line: 'Use the animation-direction vocabulary (skill reference vocabulary.json); an intent word outside it is refused.' No prompt restates the terms
after.gate: animation-vocabulary (shell_verify probe-vocabulary.py with a control): reads proposals, rulings.json, pose sheet facets and materials.json; every intent word resolves; a planted word 'vibey' is refused
after.rulingForm: D<N>, <who>, <date>: <verb> <object> <value> because <intent word> (ref <card id>) (closes p<NNN>) — parsed by compile-bible into rulings.json fields verb/object/value/intent/ref
after.interviewForm: one question per turn: situation (what the page shows at a frame) · the options as vocabulary words · the default · what lane or property it changes · the reference card; the director files it as a proposal of kind owner-ask and the owner rules it on the page
after.materials: every property value carries an intent word from the material domain (snap, float, weighted, drape, crisp, soft) and a reference; presets per acting register (warm-playful, reverent, focused) so a register ruling sets a whole family of values; the bench prints the intent word beside the measured curve
after.ledger: eagle_board.py apply already records reference -> contract change; the same ledger entry is written for a material or ruling change, so 'what led to what' is one query

unanchored.text: original blue terminal-faced Codex and coral Claude Code Clawd accompany the human from the opening.
human is the B figure with the C layered shirt, as drawn in [human-selected-02.png](studies/human-selected-02.png). Frozen; no further regeneration.

medium is Remotion as the single substrate; the Three.js kit beat mounts inside it through `@remotion/three`. Verdict and comparison recorded in the tech_recommendation pass (chain-tech_recommendation#1).
the tool is a frame the companion holds up. Looking into it reads as nearly infinite, as if a whole other world lies inside.

the gadget is a hybrid machine in the spirit of The Midnight Gospel's universe simulator: familiar parts, an impossible whole, organic and mechanical at once. The planner first recorded this as Mind Game; the owner's word was "gospel". Not a device with buttons, not an abstract orb.

the frame interior must read as someplace else, not a flat picture. It needs refraction and diffusion: what lies behind the frame is displaced, softened and edge-shifted as through glass. A flat gradient, however rendered, fails. This moves the frame interior to a GPU pass (Three.js inside Remotion).

the world inside the frame is the entire environment, not one piece: the assembled kit standing for the gates, frameworks, prompts and resources of the script and plan. Beat 4 reveals the whole destination through the frame; beat 5 builds it one piece at a time.

shadows are intentional shapes, as on the board's sticker sheets: a drawn form shadow that follows the silhouette and a cast shadow on the field, each a designed shape with a weighted edge. A flat lower band is not a shadow.

the glass pass is the right path. Shadows keep evolving toward The Midnight Gospel's look: gradients built from dither and stipple, not smooth ramps, so a shadow reads as drawn texture while still grading across a form.

the architecture inside the frame stays organic but familiar to the workflow being solved. The meta narrative: these bots are standardizing their own design process, which is what this project is doing, and the showcase prompt chain scaffolded in the server is the evidence trail a viewer can run.

the architecture inside the world follows Dr. Seuss's Midnight Paintings (six filed in `references/seuss-*`): swooping organic towers, stacked pointed arches, curling stalks with flag leaves, pale thin contour outlines on a black field, light as beaded strings. The frame interior is constructed as receding hand-drawn frames, each slightly turned (the nested-frames painting). Their outline and silhouette language may inform new assets. Colors and the exact architecture inside the frame are provisional for this test demo; the Codex and Claude identity pigments still do not change.

the animation language is "drawn on twos, light on ones" (section below), a hybrid of The Midnight Gospel's drawn layer, CloudySky's force-with-memory light doctrine, LCSlates' material transformation and shfred's cut-driven progression; the early-web explainer tween is the named failing control.
line boil is visible, toward The Midnight Gospel's wobble, not subtle.

the opening frame is the poster. Frame 0 of the film doubles as the GitHub thumbnail, so at a glance it must say what the project is and what is about to happen: the project mark, the trio, the box, on the settled black field. The film never opens on the overwhelm state; beat 4's brightness is the end of beat 3, not the opening.

the human's skin is an identity pigment between Clawd's coral and Codex's blue, so the trio reads as a tricolor, in the mauve-pink family the Midnight Gospel and Seuss references use. Owner chose B, green `#67b479`, with A, mauve `#c885c2`, as the shadow-side step (`studies/skin-10.md`); both are identity pigments in `tokens.ts` and never grade. The trio is coral, blue, green.

no asset or approach is accepted as its first iteration. Between iterations a muse pass runs (`showcase_asset_muse`: design_muse on the filed references and the existing cast, then 3+ variants rendered side by side in the substrate as an `AssetSheet`, then a rubric grade). A variant must cite the reference properties it borrows and the cast property it sits between; the pick is the owner's and the losers stay as controls. The beat1-11 human is the failing control: a first draw that cited nothing.

the board (`references/board.json`) is a clean slate: references, laws and anti-references only. Nothing the project has drawn, no muse sheet, no study still and no failing control appears on it; those live under `studies/` and are graded against the board, never shown beside it. The previous demos are weak and are not inspiration.
no captions beyond the held title; flips on any owner word naming a beat that needs one.
frame bars gold from the nested-frames painting; flips if a still reads the frame as part of the gadget.

the production is two server chains. `showcase_preproduction` runs once per episode (board → story and beats → shot list and object inventory → package grade behind the `showcase-review` gate); the muse then runs once per object from the inventory (`showcase_asset_muse`). `showcase_shot` runs once per shot (timing table → render study → rubric grade behind the gate → evidence). The shot list `v3/shots.json` is the handoff between them.

a shot run feeds the script. The evidence step writes the measured frame range into the shot's `measured` field and into that beat's provisional range in `script.md` with a dated note; the owner's beat text is never rewritten.

a render study produces a frame set, never one still: first, key, last and a six-frame consecutive strip around the key, plus the determinism, twos/ones and identity-pigment probes, so the review grades at the evidence tier the rubric demands.

Blender is an optional path on the render study, taken only when the request names `renderer:blender` and `tool:blender_render`. It is a script tool with an explicit trigger and a confirmation, refusing with a named reason when no Blender binary is reachable (none is, in this WSL2; the Windows host is the place to run it). The server has no Blender feature of its own; script tools (`docs/guides/script-tools.md`) and the workflow `remainder` (`docs/reference/workflow-ir.md`) are the documented mechanisms this path uses.

Codex and Clawd stay as the identity anchors, but their construction may morph to match the world; they do not keep their default style. Identity pigments remain fixed (C1); silhouette, contour and shadow language follow the board like every other object, so each companion gets a muse pass whose variants cite the official sprite only for pigments and recognizable features.

the fewest cuts. Beats progress by morphs, transitions and camera moves that follow leading lines the world provides (a stalk's curl, the beaded string, the frame's edge, the structure's silhouette); a cut is a last resort and the shot row must justify it. This replaces the edit-layer rule "beats progress by cut and reframe, not by pans; the camera is locked within a beat".

hand-coded SVG characters are the wrong tool (sheets 11, 14, 15 are the failing controls). Every asset is drawn by an image model from board images as inputs, through Codex's image tool driven by `codex exec -i <ref> … -- "<prompt>"` from a script tool in the muse chain, so the bible is enforced by image input and the exact `referenced_image_paths` are receipted. The owner picks from generated sheets; the pick is cut into layers (rembg + VTracer), quantized to the five roles with identity pigments pinned, and animated as a cutout puppet in Remotion (pegs, one pivot each, on twos; blend passes multiply/screen/add over the layers; boil as generated contour variants or a seeded noise pass). Remotion stays the substrate. A style LoRA on the host GPU is HELD until twenty accepted drawings exist. Verdict and sources: tech_recommendation 2026-10-13 (chain-tech_recommendation#1); first proof `studies/drawing-source-01.png`.

`codex exec` with attached references is the default drawing source for every generated asset; the `imagegen` script tool (`media/showcase/scripts/imagegen/`) is its only entry point, so every generation carries its prompt, `referenced_image_paths`, source path and sha256.

generation covers more than characters: character sheets, silhouette explorations, environment and world-building plates, and derived maps (depth, normal) as baselines, all composed together in the substrate; gaussian splats from reference video are allowed as reference or animation input when a shot needs them. Linework is incorporated as a pass once the real scene renders, not drawn into the plate. Taste default accepted: characters quantized to five flat roles, interiors keep their painted texture.

there is no video model and there will be none; a generated still is never animated by generation. The translation layer is the contract: every generated plate is cut into layers (parts for characters, planes for environments), bound to roles, and moved programmatically by `motion.ts` under the animation language, so the bible, not the model, decides motion. A plate that cannot be cut into movable layers is rejected at the sheet step.

the human is the middle direction of `studies/human-gen-16.png`, the Swoop (diamond-shouldered top, long thin limbs, large hands, one trailing swoop of hair). The human arrives wearing the heavy Cloak (the left direction) and transitions into the Swoop; the transition is a story event, not a costume cut. Planner default for its place: the cloak falls at beat 4 when the frame rises and the human looks through it, so the Swoop builds beat 5; flips on the owner's word. The face is iterated on its own sheet (eye spacing, eye-to-mouth distance, head shape) against the states the puppet must animate (neutral, blink, mouth, look), and the pick names what the face can do.

the human's face is row 2 of `studies/human-gen-17-faces.png`: a rounded head, eyes wide apart, mouth low; its four cells (neutral, blink, open mouth, look) are the face states. Because those marks are small, every shot run ends with an identity pass: the head rendered at the shot's actual on-screen size and checked that the face and the trio's identity remain trackable; a face that vanishes at that size is fixed by enlarging the marks, never by changing the head.

cut parts are never rendered as hard nearest-colour pixel blobs. Every part carries a soft antialiased alpha (blurred mask, sigma ≈ 1.1 px at plate scale) and a pale contour halo one step lighter drawn under it (the Seuss contour, ~5 px at plate scale), with the traced vector (VTracer spline) as the alternative rendering; the rig sheet compares hard, soft+contour and vector+contour side by side before a rendering is chosen. Compared on `studies/rig-sheet-02.png` (2026-10-13): hard shows stair-stepped contours, soft and vector read as drawn lines; soft+contour is the default (keeps the stipple the vector flattens), vector reserved for parts that scale large. The puppet draws a child below its parent's z behind the parent, which is how the hair sits behind the face.

the production is pose-to-pose. Acting lives in key drawings the image model draws from a model sheet; the puppet draws nothing and only carries holds, breakdowns and inbetweens between consecutive keys, with the skeleton of `studies/tech-rig-01.md` as the registration tool when its toolchain is present. The expensive path is consolidated into sheets so it stays efficient: one model sheet per character, generated once and approved (turnaround front / three-quarter / side on one baseline at one scale, construction volumes, a proportion ruler in heads, the D70 expression states, a hands row), and one key sheet per shot and actor (every key the timing chart names, 4–8 keys on one plate at the model sheet's scale, numbered, each with its line of action) so a shot costs one generation per actor plus the regeneration of rejected keys. Timing charts are the motion contract (section below). A clean-up standard governs every plate before it is cut (section below). The rotation-only puppet of `studies/puppet-proof-02` and the hand rig of `rig-sheet-01/02` are the failing controls. Rubric C20–C23.

the world is not calm daylight. Saturated figures and objects on a black field, readable as negative space. The owner's [style board](references/style-board-2026-10-06.png) is the primary reference ([index](references/style-references.json)).

no 3D characters. The puppet becomes a 2D mesh-deformation rig (AnimatedDrawings ARAP core ported to TypeScript, rendered through @remotion/three); drawn key plates are sibling meshes on one skeleton. Decision and prior art: `studies/tech-rig-02.md`; measured target cadence: `studies/craft-ref-01.md`.

one hue pair and one emitter per shot, chosen from the owner's own Eagle saves (board-06 §7). The pair is the radiance hue plus one local accent on the black field; identity pigments never grade (C1). Shot table below; `shots.json` carries the hex pairs.

the human model sheet `studies/human-model-01.png` is approved as the identity contract (`assets/human/model.json`, `provisional: false`): three views within 0.4 %, ruler 8 heads (lower bound), expressions 7–10, hands 11–14.

the clean-up contour standard is the approved model sheet's measured line, not a fixed fraction. The generator draws a near-constant 2.8 px line at plate resolution, so a ratio moves with figure height: the pick measured 1/240 at 680 px, the approved sheet 1/166 at 470 px. Keys are compared to the model sheet at the same figure height, ± 20 %. The human's standard is therefore 1/166; `model.json` `contour.ratio` carries it and `scripts/model_measure.py --ratio` reads it.

every shot gets a cinematography sheet before its keys, one generation through `showcase_layout_sheet`: the frame at the start of the shot's move and at its end, a top-down staging plan with the camera path, the leading line the move follows (D64), the emitter and the D74 hue pair, the figure's on-screen height in heads, and the Composition cards it borrows from (board-06 §8, filed from the owner's library through /inspiration). The key sheet is drawn at this camera; the render study measures the figure's on-screen height against it (C25). The shot chain is layout → motion → keys → render → grade → evidence. Dynamic poses are tested as the shot's own keys at this camera, never as a second rig lift.

worlds and guides. Codex and Clawd guide the human (the user) through worlds the frame opens onto, each a workflow of the server in its own style: the **art world** in crayon (prompts and resources; Clawd leads), the **programming world** shaded and futuristic with emissive edges (chains and gates; Codex leads), and the **line world** as every crossing (everything reduces to its contour lines, the lines re-route along the move's leading line, then refill in the next world). Home is the Seuss black field. A world is a renderer over the one rig: keys, charts, model sheets and layouts are shared; a world changes materials, passes and backgrounds only (`src/library/worlds/`, contracts `v3/worlds/<world>.json`, a `showcase_world_sheet` per world). Identity pigments hold across worlds (C1); silhouette and line follow the world (D63).

60–70 seconds, so the server's vision is understood; the beat ledger `beats-v2.json` is the provisional story at 65 s, eight beats, six shots. `beats.json` (40 s) stays the composition's input until the shots are rebuilt. The owner is asked at named plot points (the ledger's `asks`) so pacing stays organic.

the register is warm, playful and inviting, in the spirit of Elmo (Sesame Street, Elmo's World) and its kin, where a child is met by a world that wants to play with them. Reverence is reserved for the frame rise (beat 4) and the final settle (beat 8); everywhere else the failures are gentle gags and the guides have personalities. Every pose, timing band and acting note is graded against this register first.

the human carries the audience's eyes, Clawd the heart and Codex the humour. Clawd leads by touch, Codex by gesture. The companion lean-in variants and the close framing in each world follow from this; it is a starting point, revisited once the acting is watched.

the one remembered image is not ruled yet, because pacing and impact cannot be judged without an artifact that shows the whole script at once. The chain produces an edit sheet (`v3/edit-sheet.json`, rendered to `out/edit-sheet.html` by `scripts/animation/edit-sheet.mjs`): every beat with its seconds, frames, world, guide, register, what the light pushes, keys and holds counted from the exposure sheet, a frame from the latest animatic, the open asks, and the shift every later beat takes when a beat's seconds change. The owner edits and iterates on that sheet; the ruling on the one image waits for it.

the lighting always acts in favour of the emotional impact, and the scene is composed to support what the lighting pushes, never the other way around. The light script is upstream of blocking and poses: each beat names the feeling its light drives, and the layout and pose steps read that line before they place anything. The emitter tints, the arrival intensity and the crossing fade are judged by whether they push that feeling.

timing and acting references are named on the board, not implied: Kyle Baker and Genndy Tartakovsky for holds and snaps, Studio Ghibli for weight on contact, and Ghibli's habit of drawing the details only a child would notice, so the world reads as lived in and the detail builds character. Each is filed with its facets and a why; the timing bands in the chain are re-cut against them.

the one remembered image is the frame rise, beat 4: the human small and lit from inside the frame, the cloak falling. Beat 4 takes 10 s (from 6), the art and programming worlds 10 s each (from 12); the total stays 65 s. The first pose work of animatic 04 goes to beat 4, and the ending stays wide and small by contrast.

the production bible. One compiled document `v3/bible.json` (OpenTimelineIO-shaped: named tracks over the frame axis, flat, copied, never hand-edited) joining pacing, script, blocking, camera, keys, light, colour script, look and proposals; one read-only page `out/bible.html` with a frame cursor that reads every lane at that frame, the colour strip and the animatic frame; proposals as records in `v3/proposals/` anchored to a beat or frame with before and after, kind (change, inspiration, eureka, owner-ask, finding), status and the ruling that closed them (Kitsu's version-and-frame-anchored review, borrowed as a shape); `probe-bible.py` with a control as the gate; the chains' evidence and muse steps write proposals into it. The director answers the owner through proposals. The beat-4 action proposed in round two is proposal p001 and is unruled until it is read on the page. Recommendation receipt: chain-tech_recommendation#1 (2026-10-18).

the bible is also the editing system before any further ruling. A local server on the preview port serves the page and accepts its edits, patching the one JSON file each belongs to and rebuilding through `npm run bible` so no edit bypasses the probe; the page edits beat boundaries by dragging on the pacing lane, seconds, register, light intent and actions inline, files a proposal or an inspiration at the cursor, and rules a proposal with the next D-number written into this list; the chains' evidence and muse steps file their findings and picks as proposals (row 7.5). Round two resumes only when all of that is built.
